title: Two clients, one OBS — passive detection of go-live
summary: Used StartVirtualCam/StopVirtualCam (not StartStream) because it needs no network at all, so it cannot accidentally reach anything real, and it fires VirtualcamStateChanged with the same outputActive/outputState shape StreamStateChanged uses. Client A (passive) saw active=true, inactive=true without calling Start/StopVirtualCam itself. Scene switch from A while B connected: ok=true. Both clients still connected after: true.

title: Crop-to-fill is buildable
summary: Used color_source_v3 sized 1920x1080 as the 16:9 stand-in (no camera assumed attached on this machine). SetSceneItemTransform with boundsType OBS_BOUNDS_NONE + cropLeft/cropRight + scaleX/scaleY filled the 1080x1920 canvas: resulting item width=3413.333251953125 height=1920 (want 1080x1920).

title: Text overlay updates live; show/hide on a timer
summary: Input kind used: text_gdiplus_v3. SetInputSettings with settings key "text" updated live (readback matched=true). SetSceneItemEnabled toggled off then back on (final enabled=true).

title: Transitions available; cut + 300ms fade reachable
summary: Stock transition kinds installed: 2. Set current transition to "Fade" @300ms: true. A stinger transition kind is offered by GetTransitionKindList (kind id "obs_stinger_transition") — obs-websocket has no CreateSceneTransition request, so a stinger can only be added as an instance of that kind through the OBS UI (or by writing it into the scene collection JSON before launch) on first run, then just referenced by name over the API afterwards; the API itself cannot author one from a video file at runtime.

title: Preview cost (GetSourceScreenshot, 270px wide)
summary: 2fps target: achieved 1.96fps, OBS CPU ~0.4%, probe CPU ~0.0%. 5fps target: achieved 4.91fps, OBS CPU ~0.4%, probe CPU ~0.0%.

title: Media playback end event (lowest priority — music is out of MVP)
summary: MediaInputPlaybackEnded fired for a 0.5s non-looping ffmpeg_source: true. Last GetMediaInputStatus: {"mediaCursor":null,"mediaDuration":null,"mediaState":"OBS_MEDIA_STATE_ENDED"}. The event is enough; no polling needed.

title: Canvas 1080x1920 + the OBS-restart-after-canvas-change quirk
summary: SetVideoSettings to 1080x1920 confirmed immediately via GetVideoSettings; after a full OBS quit + relaunch on the same profile it still reports 1080x1920 base / 1080x1920 output (survived=true). Collection preserved across restart: false. Our first-run flow does need to bake in a restart after the first canvas set, matching Whatnot's own quirk — but the setting itself is a persisted profile property, not something we need to re-apply every launch.
